If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the mid-horizon (days 15–25) to account for overconfidence.

If sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the late-horizon (days 25–30) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add a 0.5–1% upward bias to forecast in the early horizon (days 1–10) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1% from forecast in the early horizon to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% in the late horizon to reflect market exhaustion or reversal.

If sentiment drops to -0.33 or below in the last 2 days, increase forecast by 1–3% in the mid-horizon to anticipate rebound or reversal.
